analysis.title: Flash Crash: Kioxia Warns NAND Price Surge Ending, Sending Sandisk Plunging
key_insights: Sandisk beat on revenue and EPS with 85.1% gross margin, guided above the Street, announced $5B more buybacks and an 8-for-1 split effective November 20, yet the stock was flat after hours.

At 5:54am ET Bloomberg reported Kioxia guided operating profit below estimates and said the surge in flash prices was easing. Sandisk fell as much as 8% premarket to $1,197.57, down 16% from Wednesday's high of $1,419. Micron fell in sympathy.

Kioxia guided December-quarter operating profit of ¥2 trillion ($12.7B) against consensus of ¥2.35 trillion. That implies roughly zero growth after a 57% sequential jump in the September quarter. Consensus had assumed about 18% growth.
NAND average selling price rose a mid-20% in the three months to September, versus 70% in the prior quarter. Prices are still rising, at roughly a third of the earlier pace.

Kioxia's September quarter operating profit rose 22-fold y/y to ¥1.99 trillion, in line with estimates, on revenue of about ¥2.48 trillion (+40% QoQ). It declared its first-ever interim dividend of ¥90 per share.

Kioxia executives warned against excessive price rises for fear of alienating customers. Intel guided to a ~12% drop in PC units this year and ~10% in 2027, citing memory constraints. Intel stock fell 25%.

The article says NAND spot prices stopped rising in March and are at 7-month lows, while contract prices kept climbing for two more quarters because they reset with a lag. It argues the next contract reset leans lower.

Supply is expanding: Kioxia and Sandisk plan more than ¥5 trillion of Japanese capacity over six years, with a US ADR listing next year that could raise at least $10B. Micron is building a $24B Singapore NAND fab, YMTC holds 13% of global NAND, and CXMT is entering flash.
Goldman's Giuni Lee said Samsung's NAND profit was slightly lower than Goldman expected, on slightly lower bit shipments and ASP.
Sandisk FQ1 results per Goldman: revenue $11.03B (GS $11.22B, Street $10.74B), gross margin 85.1% (GS 85.7%, Street 84.9%), non-GAAP EPS $49.51 (GS $49.80, Street $46.73).

Sandisk guided FQ2 revenue to $12.4B at the midpoint (GS $13.55B, Street $12.08B) and non-GAAP EPS to $55-57 (GS $59.71, Street $52.94). The guide beat the Street but fell well below Goldman, which the article reads as a proxy for buyside whisper numbers.

Datacenter is roughly half of industry bit demand (up from ~20% in 2020) and 43.5% of Sandisk's FY1Q27 mix. Sandisk expects KV cache to be ~35% of the AI datacenter market by 2030 and datacenter to exceed 55% of the NAND market in CY27.

Goldman's Jim Schneider says long-term agreements cover ~50% of planned FY27 and 65% of FY28 bit capacity, unchanged from August despite two more deals (10 agreements with 8 unique customers). Floor pricing is a cushion, but about half of next year's bits are exposed to contract pricing.
Schneider remains a buyer, saying the NAND market sees very limited supply additions. He raised CY26-CY28 EPS estimates ~7%. $10.5B remains on the buyback authorization.

Slower NAND price increases would ease memory-driven inflation in PCs, phones and servers, which is favorable for CPI and PC makers and negative for memory stocks. The article notes Fed Chair Warsh blamed rising rates for hammering AI stocks.

Article's view: the mid-20s price growth is the next stop on the way down, not the bottom. Hyperscalers, with $750B of AI spending colliding with slowing core growth, may negotiate harder. Goldman hosts Korea and Japan memory analysts Sunday evening, and its China desk was still a buyer of memory overnight.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's Schneider remains a buyer on very limited NAND supply additions and raised CY26-CY28 EPS ~7%. The stock fell about 7-8% premarket despite the beat after Kioxia's guidance.
Micron fell in sympathy with Sandisk after Kioxia's guide miss. Goldman called it a further negative datapoint for memory and semis.
Intel fell 25% after guiding PC units down ~12% this year and ~10% in 2027, blaming memory prices and constraints.
The memory ETF was down 5.6% premarket per JPMorgan's Market Intel desk, on renewed AI monetization fears.

sector_views.rationale: The article expects NAND contract price growth to keep slowing as supply expands and PC and phone makers cut units. Goldman's TMT desk calls Kioxia's guide a further negative datapoint, though its analyst Schneider stays a buyer of Sandisk.

earnings_insights: Sandisk FQ1 27 (reported 10/29): revenue $11.03B reported vs GS est $11.22B and Street (Visible Alpha) est $10.74B. Gross margin 85.1% vs GS est 85.7% and Street est 84.9%. Non-GAAP EPS $49.51 reported vs GS est $49.80 and Street est $46.73.
Sandisk FQ2 guidance: revenue midpoint $12.4B vs GS est $13.55B and Street est $12.08B. Non-GAAP EPS $55.00-$57.00 (midpoint $56.00) vs GS est $59.71 and Street est $52.94.

Kioxia FQ (Sept quarter, reported after the Tokyo close 10/29): operating profit ¥1.99 trillion reported, in line with estimates, up 22x y/y. Revenue about ¥2.48 trillion, up 40% QoQ. December-quarter operating profit guide of ¥2 trillion vs consensus est ¥2.35 trillion.
Samsung NAND profit reported overnight was slightly lower than Goldman's estimate, per Goldman's Giuni Lee (slightly lower bit shipments and ASP).
Intel guided to a ~12% decline in PC units this year and ~10% in 2027, citing memory constraints, and fell 25%.
Goldman's Schneider raised CY26-CY28 EPS estimates for Sandisk by ~7%.

macro_indicators.reading: mid-20% QoQ in the three months to September vs 70% in the prior quarter
macro_indicators.interpretation: Contract prices are still rising but at about a third of the prior pace, which points to slowing memory price inflation.
The guide implies roughly flat profit sequentially and signals a deceleration in the NAND pricing cycle.
Memory costs are reducing PC demand, so customers are pushing back on pricing.

risk_factors: NAND contract price growth slowing from 70% to the mid-20s, with spot prices at 7-month lows and contract prices lagging spot.
Capacity additions: Kioxia/Sandisk more than ¥5 trillion over six years, Micron's $24B Singapore fab, YMTC at 13% share, CXMT entering NAND, and a possible $10B+ Kioxia US ADR raise.
Customer pushback on memory prices, shown by Intel and PC and smartphone OEMs cutting units.
About half of Sandisk's FY27 bit capacity is not covered by long-term agreements and is exposed to contract pricing.
Hyperscalers may negotiate harder if Big Tech's $750B AI spending collides with slowing core growth.
Elevated expectations: the article cites Goldman's August framing of supportive fundamentals but very high expectations.
vol_and_positioning: Sandisk fell as much as 8% premarket to $1,197.57, down 16% from Wednesday's high of $1,419.
The memory ETF (DRAM) was down 5.6% premarket per JPMorgan's Market Intel desk.

Kioxia's stock had already fallen about 60% from its June peak before the print, and it has returned 2,400% since its December 2024 IPO per Goldman's Jay Narain. Its results came after the Tokyo close, so holders carry the position through the weekend.
The article says the memory trade peaked June 25 and Kioxia had retraced 40% from its peak by July 27.

tension_points.bull_case: Mid-20% quarterly contract price growth is still extraordinary, datacenter is about half of NAND bits, and Kioxia's management may be conservative to avoid alienating customers. Goldman's Schneider sees very limited supply additions, and Goldman's China desk was still a buyer.
tension_points.bear_case: Contract price growth fell from 70% to the mid-20s, spot peaked in March, and supply is expanding across Kioxia/Sandisk, Micron, YMTC and CXMT. PC and phone OEMs are cutting units, and about half of Sandisk's FY27 bits are not under long-term agreements.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bear view weakens if the next contract reset holds price growth at or above the mid-20s, or if hyperscaler demand absorbs new supply without pushback.

theme_stances.key_argument: Contract price growth fell from 70% to the mid-20s while spot prices peaked in March and supply is expanding, so the next stop is lower.
